label: conj:complex-chirality-rotation
title: Chirality as continuous phase rotation in the pre-observable sector
html:
Conjecture. Chirality as continuous phase rotation in the pre-observable sector

Let q = |q|e^{i\theta} be a complex substrate parameter with |q| > 1 and \theta \in (-\pi, \pi] (complex substrate interpretation).

Conjecture. In the pre-observable sector (before the dagger positive-definiteness axiom), the phase \theta controls the particle-antiparticle distinction:

  1. Crossing energy phase. For a torus knot T_{p,k} with crossing energy \mathcal{S}_c(T_{p,k}; q), the complex extension is:

      \mathcal{S}_c(T_{p,k}; |q|e^{i\theta})
  = 
  \mathcal{S}_c(T_{p,k}; |q|)e^{in_c\theta},

    where n_c is the crossing number. The mirror T_{p,k}^{\sigma} carries crossing number -n_c, so \mathcal{S}_c(T_{p,k}^{\sigma}) = \mathcal{S}_c(T_{p,k}; |q|)e^{-in_c\theta}.

  2. Chirality interpolation. The chirality operator \mathcal{X}_\varphi \colon \theta \mapsto \theta + \varphi acts on the phase of q:

    • \varphi = 0: Identity action.
    • \varphi = \pi / n_c: Particle and antiparticle crossing energies equalize in magnitude and oppose in phase.
    • \varphi = \pi: Full chirality reversal (q \mapsto |q|e^{i(\theta + \pi)}).

    The discrete electron/positron flip (chirality remark) is the endpoint \varphi = \pi of this rotation.

  3. CPT as \mathbb{Z}_2 quotient. The observable sector (\theta = 0) detects only the \mathbb{Z}_2 quotient of this \mathrm{U}(1) action. Charge conjugation C is the residue of continuous chirality rotation. Parity P and time reversal T descend from pre-observable continuous operations. The CPT theorem means the total rotation \mathcal{X}_\pi \circ P \circ T is a symmetry of the categorical action (categorical action).

Experimental discriminant. Any pre-observable phase \theta surviving in the observable sector appears as a CP-violating phase in crossing-energy ratios. For the electron-positron system:

  \delta_{\mathrm{CP}}
  = 
  \frac{|\mathcal{S}_c(T_{2,3})| - |\mathcal{S}_c(T_{2,3}^{\sigma})|}{|\mathcal{S}_c(T_{2,3})| + |\mathcal{S}_c(T_{2,3}^{\sigma})|}
   \sim 
  \mathcal{O}(\theta^2).

This vanishes to first order, matching electron-positron mass equality. It contributes at second order to hadronic CP violation, where multiple crossing numbers interact.
